source_text: Quod ceteris apostoli Pauli Epistolis difficilior putatur ad intelligendum haec quae ad Romanos scripta est, duabus mihi videtur fieri ex causis. Una, quod elocutionibus interdum confusis et minus explicitis utitur; alia, quod quaestiones in ea plurimas movet, et eas praecipue quibus innitentes haeretici astruere solent quod uniuscujusque gestorum causa non ad propositum debeat, sed ad naturae diversitatem referri. Deprecantes Deum qui docet hominem scientiam, explanationis Epistolae Pauli ad Romanos contingemus exordium.
pass_a_gloss: That this which is written to the Romans is thought harder to understand than the rest of the apostle Paul’s epistles seems to me to happen for two causes. One, that he sometimes uses confused and less explicit expressions; another, that he raises many questions in it, and especially those on which heretics lean to assert that the cause of each person’s deeds ought not to be referred to purpose but to diversity of nature. Entreating God who teaches man knowledge, we shall reach the beginning of the explanation of Paul’s Letter to the Romans.
pass_b_english: Romans is reckoned harder than Paul’s other letters for two reasons: tangled phrasing, and many questions — especially those heretics twist to deny free purpose and blame [[diversity of nature >> Bible:Romans 9:11-21]]. We ask the God who [[teaches man knowledge >> Bible:Psalm 94:10]] and gives [[a word of wisdom by the Spirit >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:8]] before we open the letter.
notes: True OET; no Scheck FOTC Romans.
